title: `actl new --revise N` can also change N's dependencies and group (GitHub issue #9)
objective: An opener revision of ticket N can change N's depends_on and group in the same write as its ticket fields, under the refusals of `actl dag` except the 'mentions #M' one.
outline: ticket_creator.py: apply_revised (a worker or other non-user 'revised') and user_reset (a user or main 'revised' through _revise) take the hand-in's 'dag' and call core/dagedit inside the same change, after the ticket fields, state and leave_group are applied; _revise fills new reviser.md placeholders (state, group, depends_on and the dag paragraph only for source user or main). Do not change decide() or ack(): the page-ack ticket changed them. prompts/reviser.md: the 'dag' paragraph behind a placeholder.
test_plan: Verifier: acceptance 4 (a)-(e) in a new class `ReviseDagAcceptance(LoopCase)` in tests_devloop/test_opener.py, placed between the existing classes T12Acceptance and LastFullSecondsUnit; the fake action 'revised_dag' is the verifier's (the implementer does not add it); FAKE_REVISE_DAG is set in self.env. Expected values from this ticket. Implementer: acceptance 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 in a new class between LastFullSecondsUnit and OpenerGroupChoice in test_opener.py. Run only test_opener, test_pages, test_issuer, test_dag_edit, test_groups and the base set.
notes: Group new-g2, last: it depends on the `actl dag` ticket for core/dagedit.py. The 'mentions #M' refusal is left out here on purpose: `actl dag` sends that case to this path so the opener judges it (D-096 item 3). Never write the reporting project's name in code, tests or comments (tests/test_no_project_names.py forbids it in every non-markdown file): say 'the reporting project'.
acceptance: A reviser hand-in of kind 'revised' may carry 'dag': {'depends_on': [ids], 'group': '<open group id>' or 'new'}, each key optional (depends_on replaces N's whole list; an absent key leaves that part unchanged). It is applied through devloop/core/dagedit.py (from the `actl dag` ticket) in the same pool write as the ticket fields, with the `actl dag` events, by 'opener' and why the hand-in's note.

Refusals are `actl dag`'s for the resulting change, checked on the ticket as it is after the revision's own changes (a user or main decision turns a stuck ticket ready in that same write, so its DAG may change), except the 'mentions #M' refusal: the opener is the judge D-096 names. A worker's revision (its ticket is running) with a 'dag' part is refused. A refused 'dag' part writes nothing of the revision: the command prints 'REVISE FAILED: <the refusal line>' and exits 1, and a user decision's --page stays unread (as for an unusable answer today).
devloop/prompts/reviser.md: for --from user or main the prompt shows N's state, group and depends_on and describes the 'dag' key; for a worker's revision it says nothing of 'dag'.

Cases, with a fake creator action 'revised_dag' that the verifier adds to tests_devloop/fake_agent.py as its own elif branch next to 'revised', with a comment; it hands in {'kind': 'revised', 'ticket': {'acceptance': ['a possible thing']}, 'cases_wrong': false, 'note': 'dag changed', 'dag': json.loads($FAKE_REVISE_DAG)}. (a) Stuck #1 in open g1, ready #2 in open g2, FAKE_REVISE_DAG '{"depends_on": ["2"]}': `ticket_creator.py --revise 1 --from main --decision revise --reason x` exits 0; #1 is ready with acceptance ['a possible thing'] and depends_on ['2']; #1's events include 'dag: depends on #2' with by 'opener'; core.chain.order is ['g2', 'g1']. (b) The same with '{"group": "new"}': #1 is in a new group g3 whose members are ['1']. (c) '{"depends_on": ["9"]}' (no #9): exit 1, stdout contains 'REVISE FAILED' and '#9 does not exist'; #1's fields, state and dag.json entry are unchanged (the 'user answer' event that decide() writes first stays, as today). (d) A mentioned dependency may be dropped here: #1's objective mentions '#2', #1 depends on #2, '{"depends_on": []}': exit 0, depends_on []. (e) A worker's revision: #1 running, `ticket_creator.py --revise 1 --from worker --reason x` with '{"depends_on": []}' exits 1, stdout contains 'REVISE FAILED' and '#1 is running'; #1 unchanged.

devloop/README.md: the sentence 'A ticket's group is not an editable field: the reviser cannot change it.' is replaced by one saying the reviser may change depends_on and group through the hand-in's 'dag' (the refusals of `actl dag`, except 'mentions #M'), and the `actl dag` paragraph names `actl new --revise N` as the route for a mentioned dependency.
Unchanged: a revised hand-in without 'dag' behaves as today (the existing revise cases in test_opener.py, test_pages.py and test_issuer.py pass unchanged).
token_basis: two ticket_creator.py functions and the reviser prompt, reusing core/dagedit.py; 5 opener subprocess cases with the fake creator; calibrated on landed complex tickets #113 (4.0M), #117 (6.8M), #119 (7.6M)

## Issue #8: a regression's deadline starts when it has the machine
Observed in T (2026-11-23): g57's full regression waited for the machine behind g56, then had about 10 minutes left; the unit layers ran 554 s, test_browsers was stopped at the deadline after 40 s and the run was `unmeasured`.
Today devloop/regression.py `verify()` passes `began + regression_timeout_seconds` to `take`/`take_machine` and gives `_verify` the time left, so the wait is charged to the run (the module docstring says so).
Wanted: `regression_timeout_seconds` limits the run from the moment the slot or the whole machine is taken (preflight, quick, full and the flaky rerun share it). The wait for the machine gets its own limit: reuse an existing setting if one fits, otherwise add `devloop.regression_wait_seconds` with a default long enough for a full regression of another group to finish (say so in devloop/README.md); a wait that runs out is `unmeasured` with a summary saying it never got the machine, as today. Update the docstring.

## Issue #10: pages close when their subject is handled from any path
Observed in T (2026-11-23): the board showed 35 open pages, every one already answered or superseded: a group's "unmeasured" page after `actl tickets rerun gN`, tickets' "stuck" pages after `actl tickets ready N`, a fixer question after the group was readied, every `created` page.
Wanted:
- An action on a subject (a ticket or a group), through any path (CLI, board, `actl new --revise ... --decision`, `tickets ready`, `tickets rerun`, `tickets release`, `cancel`), acks every open decision/env page of that subject that the action answers, recording `acked_by` as the path (e.g. "tickets ready").
- When a subject moves on by itself (a stuck ticket is running again, an unmeasured group runs a regression again, a group or ticket lands or is cancelled), its older decision/env pages are acked with `acked_by: "superseded"`.
- `created` pages are information: the board's 要你判 tab and the waiting count do not count them (they stay listed in `tickets inbox`).
- Opener: grep every place that writes or reads `acked`, and every test that asserts pages stay open; list the tests that change.

## Issue #11: a controller restart does not kill in-flight regressions
Observed in T (2026-11-23 13:52Z): stopping `actl run --forever` and starting it again left g58 and g59 with "regression unmeasured - None" pages and no regression.py running; the g57 auto_fixer survived and was adopted. Jobs are started by osx.spawn with start_new_session=True, so the cause is not known.
Wanted: first reproduce it with the loop harness (start a controller, let it start a regression with a slow fake `full`, stop the controller with SIGTERM and with SIGINT, start a new one) and find the cause; write it in the ticket. Then fix it so a running regression survives the restart and is adopted like an auto_fixer: the new controller waits for it and reads its result. If the cause turns out to be outside A (for example how the user stopped the process on macOS), say so and make the controller report it instead of writing "unmeasured - None" (the page names what happened to the job).
